C14 and C18 share parts of the anti-Communist freedom rhetoric, but neither matches the child's combination of Eastern European persecution, religious repression, suffering, and public moral support as closely.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The calculated repression of all religious organization in the Communist States","parent_excerpt":"the loss of freedom, civil rights and human dignity, the corruption of the cultural heritage of the Czechs and Slovaks, and the repression of religious life","explanation":"Both specifically characterize Communist rule in an Eastern European country as systematic repression encompassing religion and fundamental freedoms."},{"child_excerpt":"the religious spirit of man will never be subdued or extinguished, and that it will remain a sustaining force Poland during the present tragic suffering of the Polish people","parent_excerpt":"this anniversary continues to symbolize the historic devotion of the people of Czechoslovakia to democratic and humanist ideals","explanation":"Each asserts that Communist repression cannot extinguish the captive nation's sustaining commitment to spiritual or humanistic ideals."},{"child_excerpt":"this Government continue to take all appropriate steps to see to it that Communist violations of the inalienable rights of man under God do not go unopposed, and that they are effectively exposed in every forum","parent_excerpt":"We are seeing to it that the people of Czechoslovakia are made aware of this joint effort and purpose, so that they may take heart and remain firm in these trying times","explanation":"The closing assurance in each letter commits the United States to active moral and informational support so Communist oppression does not pass unanswered."}]}
